note: The official 2005 Compendium and the independent 1961 Liber Usualis confirm the complete selected Roman text and its numerari reading. The 1902 Breviarium confirms the remaining 193 words and witnesses the historical munerari reading at w130; the distinct word is excluded from that witness's same-reading coverage rather than silently normalized. Chant marks, gestures, kneeling directions, headings, following versicles and accidental punctuation are not spoken tokens.

recensional_comparators.comparator: Breviarium Romanum (1902), between the same-reading spans breviarium-1902-a and breviarium-1902-b
recensional_comparators.ruling: Select numerari because the official 2005 Compendium and the 1961 Liber Usualis independently agree on 'to be numbered'. Preserve the 1902 munerari, 'to be rewarded or endowed', as a genuine earlier Roman variant rather than an orthographic difference.
